claims.text: Integrating enhanced free-energy sampling with tailored thermal treatments will improve control of phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys.
Targeting metastable states and transformation barriers enables improved phase control.
The initial Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloy is as-processed or multiphase.
The alloy has a complex free-energy landscape containing multiple concurrent phases.
Metadynamics or umbrella sampling can map the alloy's free-energy landscape.
Enhanced sampling can identify critical metastable states and energy barriers in the alloy.
Free-energy mapping can inform the design of solution treatment, annealing, and controlled-cooling schedules.
The presence and distribution of metastable phases and their free-energy barriers mediate phase transformations.
Advanced sampling reveals key metastable states and energy barriers in the system's free-energy topography.
Tailored thermal treatments can overcome selected free-energy barriers.
Barrier-informed thermal treatments can selectively promote or inhibit specific phase transformations.
Selective promotion or inhibition of phase transformations can steer the microstructure toward a desired state.
The proposed approach will produce a controlled and targeted phase composition.
The proposed approach will produce a more predictable phase distribution than standard thermal treatments.
The proposed approach will improve material performance relative to standard thermal treatments.
Standard thermal processing that does not use free-energy-landscape information typically gives less-controlled phase distributions.
The approach depends on accurate prediction of the free-energy landscape.
Experimental uncertainty in translating computational predictions into thermal processing may limit the approach.
Differences in phase distribution and mechanical properties between tailored and conventional treatments can test the hypothesis.
